issue.title: Spawn with controllers, extra tags, and minted roster team tags
issue.body:
## Background

FTS-6D of #2496, Phase 9, `critical path`, `depends on #2551` (FTS-6C),
which must merge first. After FTS-3 every spawn still enters through the
legacy faction string, and after FTS-6C scripts can mint owner-scoped tags.
This slice moves the spawn sources onto the profile ingress: a spawn passes
an optional controller and extra tags, the colony roster carries a minted
roster team tag, location content spawns as its definition's culture under
a per-location occupant group tag, and legacy strings keep working. Those
two minted group tags are what FTS-6E's Attack orders and FTS-6A's reports
name (D-34, D-37).

Verified on `master` `2479d9543` (2026-09-07):

- **One ingress, string only.** `unit.spawn(defName, gx, gy, [gz],
  [factionId], [pageId], [bindGen])` takes a faction string in slot 4 or 5
  (`src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/Units/Spawn.hs:57`); FTS-3 (#2515) maps
  it through D-26 against the definition's defaults and keeps the argument
  list unchanged.
- **Three production sources.** The portal roster spawns five acolytes and
  a technomule with `"player"` (`scripts/building_spawn.lua:48`, `:228`);
  location content spawns each `contents` unit entry with `entry.faction
  or "hostile"` (`scripts/locations.lua:448`, `spawnUnitContent`, recording
  `{uid, home_x, home_y}` per occupant); the debug overlay passes
  `"debug"` (`scripts/init_mouse.lua:200`). The only shipped content entry
  is `ruin_small`'s `nomad_primitive` with an explicit `faction: hostile`
  (`data/locations/ruin_small.yaml:123`).
- **Locations have a stable instance identity.** `LocationInstance.liId ∷
  LocationInstanceId` (`src/Location/Instance.hs:142`, an `Int`) reaches
  Lua as `instance_id` (`WorldQuery/Location.hs:251`), so an occupant group
  tag can be derived from it deterministically.
- **Load reconciliation has a precedent.** `fromUnitSnapshot` reconciles
  saved equipment against the current definition on every staged load
  (#2307), logging per migrated entry and never failing the load; D-34's
  roster-tag backfill follows the same footing.
- **Gates.** `Portal spawn page binding (#1686)`, `persistent ruin
  encounter AI (#916)`, `Unit faction profile wire`, `Lua faction profile
  API`, and the probes `location_content_probe`, `portal_location_probe`,
  `expedition_loop_probe`, and `expedition_retrieval_probe` cover these
  sources today; the retrieval probe is a known flake (re-run first).

Owner decisions 2026-09-07: spawn sources may name only the engine's local
controller, under one documented name, in this slice; any other controller
value is inert. Roster and occupant group tags follow D-34 and D-37.

## Requirements

1. `unit.spawn` accepts, in place of the legacy string, a profile request
   naming an optional controller and optional extra tags with an owner.
   The legacy string forms keep their exact FTS-3 meaning; omitted means
   definition defaults. A request naming any controller other than the
   documented local one, a malformed tag, or a wrong-typed owner is inert:
   the unit spawns with definition defaults, `unit.spawn` reports the
   refusal once for that request, and nothing else changes.
2. Every unit the local controller owns carries one roster team tag, minted
   under the ingress's own owner identity and derived from the controller:
   the portal roster spawns with it, and a saved local-controller unit
   that lacks it gains it during load reconciliation with one log line per
   backfilled unit and never a load failure. Ordinary runtime owners cannot
   remove it.
3. Location content spawns each unit under its definition's default tags
   with no controller, plus one occupant group tag per location instance
   minted under the location's owner identity and derived from
   `instance_id`. An entry's explicit legacy `faction` string still maps
   through D-26 for the affiliation, and the occupant group tag is added
   regardless. The shipped `ruin_small` entry drops `faction: hostile`, so
   `nomad_primitive` arrives as `nomad` plus its occupant tag.
4. Relation outcomes for shipped content follow the catalogue: nomad
   occupants are hostile to acolytes through the base table, neutral to
   wildlife, allied among their own location's occupants through the
   shared tag, and neutral to another location's occupants. No consumer
   changes; the FTS-5 authority already answers this.
5. The debug overlay keeps `"debug"`; portal, location, and debug behavior
   for ownership, commandability, and discovery is otherwise unchanged.
6. The same definition spawned as location content and as a local-roster
   unit has identical authored identity and different ownership, roster
   tag, and relation outcomes, proving D-1 end to end.
7. Provenance and persistence: roster and occupant tags persist with their
   owners through FTS-3's wire without a format change; the location YAML
   boundary documents the new `faction` semantics; `scripts/CLAUDE.md`
   names the two minted group tags and their owners.

## Acceptance

A new headless spec whose top-level describe is exactly `Faction spawn
ingress` covers: every legacy string form still mapping as FTS-3 specified;
the profile request with the local controller, with extra tags, and with an
unknown controller, malformed tag, and wrong-typed owner, each refusal
inert and reported once; the roster tag present after a portal spawn and
after loading a fixture save whose units lack it; occupant tags distinct
per location instance and shared within one; and requirement 6's identity
versus ownership contrast. The ruin encounter spec gains a case that
occupants are hostile to acolytes, neutral to wildlife, and allied with
each other.

```bash
cabal build all
cabal build synarchy-test-headless
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Faction spawn ingress"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Portal spawn page binding"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "persistent ruin encounter AI"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Unit faction profile wire"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Lua faction profile API"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Location discovery"'
python3 tools/test_lua_registration_audit.py && python3 tools/lua_registration_audit.py
python3 tools/test_location_content_probe.py
python3 tools/unicode_operator_audit.py
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only location_content_probe
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only portal_location_probe
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only expedition_loop_probe
git diff --stat origin/master -- src/World/Save docs/save_compat
```

Expected: builds succeed; every spec group passes with the new group
non-empty; the audits and probe self-test exit zero; the three probes pass
one at a time; the final diff is empty (no wire change).

## Out of scope

- Any controller other than the local one, and any controller-change
  operation.
- The Attack transaction, Hold, and escalation lock: FTS-6E; reports and
  the reverse relation: FTS-6A; diplomacy resolution: FTS-6F.
- Removing the legacy string forms, `unit.getFaction`, or the adapter:
  FTS-7.
- Encounter respawning, nomad AI, or location content changes beyond the
  `faction` field.

## Related

- Epic: #2496 (FTS-6D, Phase 9, critical path). Blocked by #2551
  (FTS-6C); #2515 and #2548 are its earlier prerequisites.
- #916 (closed) authored `ruin_small`'s nomad content; #911 (closed) gave
  locations their stable instance identity; #1686 (closed) bound portal
  spawns to their page; #2307 (closed) is the load-reconciliation
  precedent.
- `docs/nomad_primitive_encounter_design.md` consumes this ingress.
- Design document (supporting detail, not required context):
  `docs/faction_tag_system_design.md`, sections "Unit-definition and spawn
  ownership", D-5, D-10, D-22, D-26, D-29, D-34, D-37.

## Automated cross-agent issue review

Reviewed against `master@c3a4cd1331ba` by GPT-6-Astra (`gpt-6-astra` at `high`).

**Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED**

Corrections and spec additions below amend the implementation spec. Supporting context is non-normative. Open decisions remain unresolved and must not be guessed.

### Corrections
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Qualify occupant tag and owner identities by (WorldPageId, instance_id), using a deterministic, collision-free representation. LocationInstanceId is allocated independently on each page, starting at 1; deriving identity from the integer alone merges unrelated groups (src/Location/Instance.hs:21–25; WorldQuery/Location.hs:171).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Update the production integration surface to include spawnEncounterUnitContent as well as spawnUnitContent. The shipped ruin_small uses count_range and therefore follows the dedicated encounter path, which independently defaults to "hostile". Preserve its registered-prefix retry behavior and the authored contents ordering (scripts/locations.lua:495, :745; data/locations/ruin_small.yaml:108–133).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Replace the blanket empty diff requirement for src/World/Save with verification that serialized shapes, component versions, and retained codecs remain unchanged. Non-wire restoration changes are legitimate: the cited reconciliation precedent lives in src/World/Save/Types.hs:876 and is consumed by src/World/Load/Stage.hs:1068.

### Spec additions / clarifications
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Exercise profile requests in both supported faction argument positions, including explicit nil Z and page/binding arguments. Preserve stale-binding refusal before allocation or queueing, and verify a mixed valid/invalid profile request applies no partial controller or extra-tag changes and logs once (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/Units/Spawn.hs:70–97; requirement 1).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Test that legacy "player" spawns also receive the canonical roster membership; ordinary runtime owners cannot remove that membership; and load backfill is idempotent, preserves existing tags and owners, and emits no backfill warning for an already-correct unit (requirements 2 and 7; design D-22 and D-34).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Add save/load coverage proving both minted tag identities and their provenance survive restoration, including equal instance integers on different pages. Use behavioral restoration evidence rather than treating the unchanged wire diff as persistence proof (requirement 7; src/World/Save/CLAUDE.md, Gates).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Prove relation outcomes through the real faction authority. The existing ruin encounter fixture supplies relation answers through a Lua stub, so merely adding expected entries to that stub cannot validate the catalogue or profile composition. Include a shared occupant-tag case with differing authored affiliations to establish that the group tag itself supplies alliance (test-headless/Test/Headless/Lua/UnitAiEncounter.hs:57; Unit/Faction/Profile.hs:435).

### Supporting context
- **GPT-6-Astra:** The checked-out SHA matches c3a4cd1331baa2f9910f3e3844f8f7ff1e58b65a. Its spawn ingress remains scalar; the missing later profile integration was evaluated under the declared-prerequisite assumption, not treated as a blocker (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/Units/Spawn.hs; dossier dependency chain).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Shared membership unconditionally supplies alliance below live causes and above base relations. This is implemented by relationFromTo and explicitly tested; tags have no separate culture/team precedence (src/Unit/Faction/Profile.hs:435–453; test-headless/Test/Headless/Unit/FactionProfile.hs:335–344; design, Directed relation precedence).

### Open decisions
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Should different locations' nomads remain allied through their shared "nomad" tag, or is cross-location neutrality an intentional policy change? Requirement 4 demands neutrality while requiring unchanged authority and preserved authored tags; those conditions cannot all hold under relationFromTo (src/Unit/Faction/Profile.hs:435–453; design D-29).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** For an explicit location faction override of "player" or "debug", does full D-26 compatibility apply, or does location spawning intentionally retain only affiliation and force no controller/capabilities? Requirement 3's unconditional no-controller wording conflicts with D-26's player mapping and requirement 5's unchanged ownership/commandability promise; the current location paths forward the supplied string unchanged (scripts/locations.lua:451, :497; design D-26).

### Recommended disposition
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Revise requirement 4 to preserve cross-location nomad alliance unless the owner explicitly chooses a separately specified policy change; distinct occupant tags still provide distinct report scopes under D-37. Resolve the explicit location-override semantics, incorporate the bounded amendments above, and rerun readiness review.

### Reviewer summaries
- **GPT-6-Astra — CHANGES REQUESTED:** The ingress work is justified, but requirement 4 contradicts the established shared-tag alliance policy. Explicit legacy location overrides also need a consistent ownership contract. The remaining integration and acceptance gaps can be resolved through amendments.
